## 维护者速读

- 改了什么:应用新增 `landing` 键,按受众声明落地页:`[{ item, visible }]`,第一个 `visible` 成立的条目决定读者打开哪个导航项;无匹配或不写时照旧打开第一个导航项。
- 为什么改:同一个应用给销售和客服共用时,只能有一个落地页;把"销售"挪到"客服"前面,客服的人一进来就落在线索上。
- 风险与回滚:只加不减,旧应用不受影响;`item` 指向不存在的导航项、或指向分组/分隔线/动作项,保存时直接拒收(不会像退役的 `homePageId` 那样悄悄落到第一项)。回滚即还原本 PR。
- 先看:`packages/spec/src/ui/app.zod.ts`(`checkAppLandingItems` 与 `AppLandingEntrySchema`)、`packages/spec/liveness/app.json`(`landing` 标为 planned 并提示作者)、`packages/lint/src/validate-expressions.ts`(落地谓词的表达式检查)。
- 两分钟验证:`pnpm --filter @objectstack/spec exec vitest run src/ui/app-landing.test.ts`,应见 14 个用例全绿,其中悬空 `item` 在 `landing.0.item` 处被拒、并列出存在的导航项 id。
- 需要你做的:无,席位落地。

## What changes

- **`AppSchema.landing`** (`packages/spec/src/ui/app.zod.ts`): an optional, non-empty list of `AppLandingEntrySchema` entries, `{ item, visible }`, both required. The console asks the entries in order and opens the first whose `visible` holds for the reader (and whose `item` the reader can see). No match, or no key: the app opens on its first navigation item by `order`, as today. The describe text states both rules.
- **The refusal the `homePageId` tombstone asked for.** `checkAppLandingItems`, a `superRefine` on `AppSchema`, runs on every app parse (so `defineApp`, `os validate` / `os build` and the metadata save door all refuse alike). It refuses, at `landing.N.item`, an `item` that names no entry of the app's own `navigation` or `areas[].navigation` (any depth through `children`), listing the openable ids that exist; and an `item` that names a `group`, `separator` or `action` entry, none of which opens a page. It also refuses, at `landing.N.visible`, a predicate that reads `data` (a landing entry has no `dataSource`), with the same lexer the navigation entry's own `data` refusal uses. It is exported (and barrel-reachable) for the same reason as `navItemVisibleDataNeedsDataSource`: a mirror attaches the function instead of restating the rule.
- **Why an id into `navigation`, not an inline target** (the order's either/or): the landing is a sidebar entry, so the sidebar can highlight what the reader landed on, and there is one copy of each navigation target. The id's old failure mode, dangling into a silent fallback, is closed by the parse-time refusal above, so the cross-reference is checked rather than trusted.
- **Why `visible` is required**: an entry with no predicate would land every reader there, which is `homePageId` again under a new name. "Open somewhere else for everyone" stays "put that entry first in `navigation`".
- **Spellings**: `landings` / `landingPages` route to `landing`; on an entry, `navigationId` / `navItem` / `itemId` / `target` / `page` route to `item`, and `visibleWhen` / `visibleOn` / `when` / `condition` to `visible`. The retired `homePageId` prescription (and its `home` / `homepage` / `landingpage` spellings) now also names `landing`, and the tombstone docblock's last paragraph says how `landing` answers both of its objections.
- **Lint** (`packages/lint/src/validate-expressions.ts`): `os validate` / `os build` judge each landing predicate with the shared validator's data-independent verdicts (CEL syntax, size, unknown function, `has()` shape). It passes no object and no `record` scope, because the slot binds no record and a `record`-scoped call would prescribe `record.FIELD`.
- **Ledgers and tables the gates force**: liveness `app.landing` row `planned` + `authorWarn` + `authorHint` (children `item`, `visible`); evaluated-slot census 32 → 33; dogfood expression-conformance row `cel-app-landing` (`experimental`, `unevaluated`); form-reconciliation `omit` row (planned, no form control); `/meta/types` `app` count 22 → 23; `dropped-refinements.baseline.json` (+1 site in six entries, the new object-level check, hand-edited per the ledger's rule); objectui census `spec-object-refinements-7715.test.ts` names `checkAppLandingItems` under `notAttachable` (test-only line, allowed by the claim amendment 6545506798), owed to the follow-up ui card.
- **Docs**: `content/docs/ui/apps.mdx` gains "Landing per audience" (shape, order rule, refusals, a Planned callout) and a property-table row; references regenerated.
- **Changeset**: `.changeset/28022-app-landing-per-audience.md`, `@objectstack/spec` and `@objectstack/lint` minor.

## Why

An app shared by more than one audience has one landing: its first navigation entry. In HotCRM, moving Sales above Service moves service staff's landing to Leads (#27386 row 5). The maintainer ruled letter A: an app-level landing list with `visible` predicates, first match wins.

## Tests

- `packages/spec/src/ui/app-landing.test.ts` (new, 14 cases): accepted shapes (top-level, nested, area-only items; bare string normalised to the CEL envelope), the control (no key parses as before), refusals at the entry's own path (dangling item listing the existing ids, `group` / `action` / `separator` targets, a `data` read, a missing `visible`, an empty list, near-miss spellings), barrel identity, and both `visible` spellings through the exported function.
- `packages/lint/src/validate-expressions.test.ts`: a non-CEL landing predicate is an error at `app 'crm' · landing[0] ('nav_leads') visible`; a healthy reader predicate is clean; the #5017 read-surface table gains `appDef` (AppSchema) and `landingEntry` (AppLandingEntrySchema), and `stack` gains `apps`.
- Ablations (one-off, then restored; restore proven by an empty `git diff HEAD`): removing the `.superRefine(checkAppLandingItems)` mount → `app-landing.test.ts` 5 failed / 9 passed; removing the lint `check(...)` call → `validate-expressions.test.ts -t landing` 2 failed (the landing case and the read-surface row).

## Acceptance notes

- **How this meets the tombstone's "enforce-first" sentence.** The maintainer ruled spec first. The liveness row is `planned` with `authorWarn`, so an author who writes `landing` is told no console applies it yet; the describe text opens with `[PLANNED — not yet rendered]`; the docs page carries a Planned callout. The tombstone's other objection, the silent dangling fallback, is closed now, at parse.
- **Not judged at the app save door: the predicate's CEL syntax.** `validateStackExpressions` does not list `app` in its `runtimeTypes`, so the lint half runs at `os validate` / `os build` only. The parse refusals (dangling item, non-opening target, `data` read, blank / `ast`-only predicate) do run at the save door. Widening the rule's runtime types is a publish-gate change, left out of this card.
- **Not judged: which roots the predicate reads.** A landing predicate reading `record.x` passes lint (no bare-identifier or root verdict on this slot). The console redirect card decides the evaluation scope; a root verdict belongs with it.
- **`navigationContributions` items cannot be named.** The refusal reads the app as parsed, and a contributed item is not part of it. Stated in the describe text and the docs.
- **Follow-up #28450:** the domain:ui landing card: the console landing redirect reads `landing`, flips the liveness row to `live`, attaches `checkAppLandingItems` to objectui's `AppComponentSchema` and drops the `notAttachable` entry, and re-classifies the `cel-app-landing` conformance row.

- [x] 1. Schemas start as Zod; `packages/spec` holds no runtime logic.
- [x] 2. Every name I added uses the casing for its kind.
- [x] 3. No formatter ran; `pnpm lint` passes (repo-wide lint is CI's run).
- [x] 4. One issue, one branch off an up-to-date `main`, one pull request.
- [x] 5. A change that publishes carries a changeset, and both declaration lines are filled in here and in the changeset.
- [x] 6. `packages/spec` touched: its generated artifacts are regenerated and committed.
- [x] 7. No hand edits to `content/docs/references/`, `packages/*/CHANGELOG.md` or `content/docs/releases/`.
- [x] 8. Title, body and comments are in English.
